make.name: XPeng
make.description: Chinese electric-car maker founded in 2014 and listed in New York and Hong Kong, known for its driver-assistance software. It delivered about 429,000 cars in 2025, sells in about 60 countries, and licenses its electrical architecture to Volkswagen. Its cheaper models are sold under the Mona name.

models.name: G3
models.description: XPeng's first production car, a compact SUV built from November 2018 (after a 15-car Identy X founders' run). Facelifted as the G3i in 2021 and exported to Norway; production ended in 2023 and the G3i was dropped from the price list in March 2025.

generations.name: G3
generations.description: Front-motor compact SUV; the 2019 update brought a 50.5 kWh standard pack and a long-range pack.

generations.name: G3i
generations.description: July 2021 facelift with a P7-style light bar and XPILOT 2.5, built in XPeng's own Zhaoqing plant.

models.name: P5
models.description: Compact sedan launched in 2021, the first mass-produced car offered with lidar. It got a facelift for 2024 and was quietly dropped in March 2025; its slot went to the Mona M03.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Front-wheel-drive sedan with 60-81 kWh packs and optional lidar.

models.name: P7
models.description: XPeng's sports sedan, delivered in China from June 2020 and exported to Europe. It was facelifted as the P7i in 2023 and replaced by an all-new second generation (E29) launched in August 2025.

generations.name: First generation (E28)
generations.description: Original P7 on the SEPA platform with a 196 kW rear motor and an AWD Performance version.

generations.name: P7i
generations.description: 2023 facelift with lidar, Orin-X driving computers and uprated motors (203 kW rear, 348 kW AWD).

generations.name: Second generation (E29)
generations.description: All-new fastback with 800-volt drive, up to 486 kW charging and XPeng's Turing chips; no lidar.

models.name: P7+
models.description: Larger, cheaper liftback sold alongside the P7, launched in China in November 2024 with XPeng's lidar-free driver assistance. A January 2026 facelift added a range-extender version (not listed here) and made it a global model built also by Magna Steyr in Graz.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Single rear motor (180 or 230 kW) with 60.7 or 76.3 kWh LFP packs; a 74.9 kWh 5C pack arrived for the 2025 Flagship trim.

generations.name: 2026 facelift
generations.description: Full-width light bar, AR head-up display, Turing chips and 5C packs; launched in China and Europe in January 2026.

models.name: G9
models.description: Mid-size SUV launched in China in 2022, XPeng's first car designed for export (Europe from 2023). A March 2025 refresh brought 5C LFP packs, more power and lidar-free driver assistance.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: 800-volt SUV with a 230 kW rear motor; AWD adds a 175 kW front induction motor.

generations.name: 2025 refresh
generations.description: New CALB 5C LFP packs (10-80% in 12 minutes), 258 kW rear motor, Turing AI driving without lidar.

models.name: G6
models.description: Mid-size coupe SUV launched in China in June 2023 and exported widely (Europe, UK from 2025, Australia, Southeast Asia). Refreshed in March 2025 with 5C batteries and a new interior.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: 800-volt SEPA 2.0 platform; China models use a 218 kW rear motor, export models 190-210 kW.

generations.name: 2025 refresh
generations.description: 81 changes: full-width light bar, 15.6-inch screen, lidar-free Turing AI driving and 5C CALB packs (10-80% in 12 minutes).

models.name: X9
models.description: Seven-seat electric MPV launched in China in January 2024 and exported to Asia and Australia. Battery packs grew in 2025; a March 2026 facelift added rear-wheel steering (a range-extender version, not listed here, arrived first).

generations.name: Original
generations.description: 800-volt MPV with a 235 kW front motor; AWD adds a 135 kW rear motor. Larger packs from April 2025.

generations.name: 2026 facelift
generations.description: Restyled bumpers, rear-wheel steering and up to three Turing chips; 94.8 kWh LFP or 110 kWh NMC.

models.name: Mona M03
models.description: Low-priced compact fastback, the first car of XPeng's Mona line, developed from a project bought from DiDi. On sale in China since August 2024; over 200,000 built by November 2025.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Front motor with FinDreams LFP blade packs; Max trims add XNGP urban driver assistance.

models.name: G7
models.description: Mid-size SUV launched in June 2025, the first car with XPeng's Turing AI chips and a Huawei-developed 87-inch AR head-up display. A range-extender version (not listed here) followed in January 2026.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: 218 kW rear motor with 68.5 or 80.8 kWh 5C LFP packs.

models.name: Mona L03
models.description: Compact coupe SUV in the Mona line, launched in China and Europe in July 2026 (sold abroad as the L03). Range-extender versions also exist and are not listed here.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Luxshare rear motor with CALB LFP packs; an AWD version is offered in Europe.

models.name: Mona L05
models.description: Mid-size fastback SUV in the Mona line, on sale in China from 29 October 2026 with first deliveries on 4 November 2026. Range-extender versions are not listed here.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Shares the L03's 246 hp rear motor with 58.2 or 71.1 kWh CALB LFP packs.

models.name: G9L
models.description: Full-size SUV launched in China in September 2026 and in eight European countries in October 2026 (built also in Graz). Despite the name it is related to the GX, not the G9. Range-extender versions are not listed here.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: 270 kW rear motor; AWD adds a 160 kW front motor. 800-volt, 5C charging.

models.name: GX
models.description: Six-seat full-size luxury SUV, XPeng's flagship, in production since March 2026 with rear-wheel steering and steer-by-wire. Range-extender versions are not listed here.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: SEPA 3.0 platform; 362 hp rear motor, AWD adds a 215 hp front motor; 91.9 kWh LFP or 110 kWh NMC.

legacy_notes.note: Labelled 'P7 Smart Sedan i' with a P7i photo, but its numbers (424 hp = 316 kW, 80 kWh) match the pre-facelift P7 AWD Performance with the 80.9 kWh pack, so it is claimed there. epa_range 244 is invented (the P7 was never EPA-rated or sold in the US); current_price 36000 has no source; drive_type 'RWD/AWD' mixes trims; generation '2023' would be the P7i. The legacy P7i photo is used for the P7i (2023) refresh row.

gaps: Prices for P7 (E28/P7i/E29), G6 2023, G7, G9 2022, Mona L03/L05 (China), G9L and GX not sourced per trim; only pre-sale ranges were found.
G9L battery sizes and per-trim ranges not sourced (EV ranges 660-755 km CLTC across four trims).
X9 2026 China: battery-to-trim pairing inferred from trim names (665/650 Max/Ultra = 94.8 kWh, 750/710 = 110 kWh); per-trim CLTC ranges not given.
G3 long-range battery quoted as both 65.5 and 66.5 kWh in sources; left null.
P5 battery per trim (60.2-80.9 kWh) not sourced; P5 2024 facelift not split out.
Mona L03 power is 246 hp in China and 241 hp (180 kW) in Europe for the same motor; 246 hp recorded.
Range-extender (EREV) versions of P7+, G6, G7, X9, L03, L05, G9L and GX deliberately excluded.
X9 Europe availability not verified; only China and Australia markets recorded.
